title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1976 notes on the divided-power (pd) de Rham complex, which this note calls DR_pd. The setting is a pd-ring (S, t, γ*): a ring S with an element t carrying divided powers γ_j(t). It has its pd-filtration Fil^i S, generated by the γ_j(t) for j ≥ i, with associated graded Gr*(S). There is a canonical surjection k{T} → Gr*(S), where k = Gr^0 S and k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra, sending T to the class of t.

(1) Comparison square. For a 'variety' 𝒳 over S there is a filtered pd de Rham complex C*_DR(𝒳; S, t, γ*). The claim is that the edge map H^i(Fil^p C*_DR) → H^i(𝒳, Fil^p S) is an isomorphism in the range i ≤ p. This holds under the standing hypothesis that k{T} → Gr*(S) is an isomorphism, i.e. that S is 'pd-regular', like a completed pd-polynomial algebra. The isomorphisms are compatible with the transition maps Fil^p → Fil^q for q ≤ p, which are iso for i ≤ q. It is a truncated comparison of filtered pd de Rham cohomology with cohomology of the filtration sheaf, of the same shape as 'Fil^r comparison in degrees ≤ r' statements in later crystalline and syntomic theory.

(2) NB: without that hypothesis nothing can be said. Two examples follow.
- (a) Extreme degeneration t = 0, so S ≅ k. Then Gr^p of the completed pd resolution Â^{*0}_* is Γ^p_k(Ψ_*), the p-th divided power applied degreewise to a (simplicial/chain) complex Ψ_*. Its homology, written H_*(k,p), is a derived-functor homology of Γ^p in the Dold–Puppe sense. This is nonzero ('not flasque') for every p ≥ 0 as soon as k ≠ 0, so no vanishing or comparison can hold.
- (b) S = Z_p with t = p and γ_j(p) = p^j/j!. Here v_p(p^j/j!) = (j(p−2)+s_p(j))/(p−1), where s_p is the digit sum.
  - For p ≠ 2 these valuations tend to infinity, so the pd-filtration defines the p-adic topology ('conforme').
  - For p = 2, v_2(2^j/j!) = s_2(j) equals 1 at powers of 2, so Fil^i Z_2 = 2Z_2 for all i ≥ 1. Then Gr*(S) = Gr^0(S) = F_2, again the degenerate case.
- Grothendieck then asks for the exact ideal S^[i] = (p^j/j!, j ≥ i). He starts to write S^[i] = (p^i/i!) and crosses it out.
- The correct answer is S^[i] = p^{m_i} Z_p with m_i = min_{j≥i} v_p(p^j/j!). The minimum is often attained at a j > i, e.g. p = 3, i = 8: v(3^8/8!) = 6 but v(3^9/9!) = 5.
- Consequently, even for Z_p with p odd, Gr*(Z_p) has gaps. For example, for p = 3, γ_2(3) = 9/2 lies in Fil^3. So k{T} → Gr* is not an isomorphism and Z_p is not 'pd-regular' in Grothendieck's sense. This is presumably the point he was approaching.
errors: The crossed-out guess S^[i] = (p^i/i!)Z_p is false in general; e.g. p=3, i=8: 3^9/9! has valuation 5 < 6 = v(3^8/8!). Grothendieck himself struck it out.
For p=2, Gr^i(S)=0 for i≥1 (not F_2); the intended statement is Gr*(S) ≅ Gr^0(S) ≅ F_2.
The comparison square is stated without proof on this page; the range i ≤ p and the exact meaning of Fil^p S on 𝒳 cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Truncated comparison: H^i(Fil^p of pd de Rham complex) ≅ H^i(X, Fil^p S) for i ≤ p, under the hypothesis that Gr of the pd-filtration of the base is a divided power polynomial algebra
ideas.modern_name: Filtered crystalline/pd de Rham comparison in a range (cf. Fil^r comparisons for i ≤ r in Fontaine–Messing, Kato syntomic theory)

ideas.what: In the degenerate case t=0, graded pieces of the completed pd resolution are Γ^p of a complex, with nonvanishing derived divided-power homology
ideas.modern_name: Derived divided powers / graded pieces of derived de Rham or derived crystalline cohomology, Gr ≅ Γ^p(L[-1])
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent II, 1972); Bhatt (p-adic derived de Rham cohomology, 2012); Dold–Puppe for derived functors of Γ^p

ideas.what: pd-filtration on (Z_p, p): defines the p-adic topology for p odd, is constant (=2Z_2) for p=2; question of the exact ideals S^[i]
ideas.modern_name: Divided power filtration on Z_p / valuations of p^j/j! (Legendre formula)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre); standard in Berthelot's crystalline cohomology

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates 'pd-regularity' of the base (k{T} ≅ Gr*(S)) as the condition making filtered pd de Rham cohomology behave, and in the degenerate case identifies graded pieces as Γ^p of a complex with nontrivial derived homology. This is the mechanism later central in derived de Rham/derived crystalline comparisons (Bhatt 2012), where graded pieces Γ^p(L[-1]) explain the comparison failure over non-smooth or degenerate pd bases.
missed.quote: Si on ne suppose pas que l'épi k{T} → Gr*(S) est un iso, on ne peut rien dire ... Gr^p Â^{*0}_* ≃ Γ^p_k(Ψ_*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck in 1976 working with simplicial/derived divided-power constructions close to derived de Rham theory. This is of historical interest, though Illusie had already defined derived de Rham complexes in 1972.

missed.claim: The question of the exact pd-filtration ideals on Z_p, and hence whether Z_p (p odd) satisfies the pd-regularity hypothesis, is left open on the page. The answer, S^[i] = p^{m_i} with m_i = min_{j≥i} v_p(p^j/j!), is elementary and shows the hypothesis fails for Z_p.
missed.quote: quelle est exactement l'idéal S^{[i]} engendré par les p^j/j! pour j ≥ i?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it explains why such comparison theorems need bases like completed pd-polynomial rings rather than (Z_p, p). This is known in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck's 1976 filtered pd de Rham theory with a truncated comparison and an explicit derived divided-power obstruction. The ideas anticipate later derived de Rham/crystalline work, but they overlap with Illusie (1972) and are standard today; the Z_p computation is elementary.
transcription_corrections: 'Gr^i(S) ≃ Gr^0(S) ≃ F_2' should read 'Gr*(S) ≃ Gr^0(S) ≃ F_2'.
Top right annotation is likely '(Iso si i ≤ p)' rather than '(Donc si i ≤ p)'.
The first line probably reads 'qui — c'est aussi' / 'Qui est aussi', not '𝓕'.
'n'est flasque pour aucun p ≥ 0 (si k ≠ 0)' is consistent with the image; 'conforme' is plausible for the p-filtration vs p-adic filtration (possibly 'confondue').
